question.text: Mr. Karthik Nair, head of operations at Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III AIF), is reviewing the fund's investment universe against Section 2(h) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act 1956 as referenced in NISM Chapter 1. Which of the following is EXPRESSLY EXCLUDED from the definition of 'securities' under SCRA?

answer.text: Units issued under a mutual fund scheme.
Unit Linked Insurance Policies (ULIPs) that combine life-insurance and investment.
Government securities and onshore rupee bonds issued by the Asian Development Bank.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 1.4.5 reproduces Section 2(h) SCRA, and clause (e) regarding mutual fund units expressly EXCLUDES 'any unit linked insurance policy or scrips or any such instrument or unit, by whatever name called which provides a combined benefit risk on the life of the persons and investment by such persons and issued by an insurer'. All other options ARE included: MF units (e), derivatives (b), government securities (h), ADB/IFC rupee bonds (i). The Trap: Option A is INCLUDED in SCRA 2(h)(e) — classic trap for candidates who confuse the carve-out (ULIPs) with the main item (MF units). Option B and D are explicitly listed as securities. Note: SCRA Section 2(h) carve-out makes ULIPs ineligible as 'securities' even though they involve investment, while derivatives, mutual-fund units, government securities, and specified multilateral rupee bonds are included. A Cat III managed-futures fund buying ULIPs would breach its PPM investment universe.
